functionality.rationale: An incorrect publication sequence can mark unpushed or remotely failing work done, or can advance the protected integration branch before its exact SHA is verified.

security.rationale: The CI client uses GitHub credentials and must avoid exposing tokens while rejecting unauthenticated, mismatched, or forged workflow evidence.

performance.rationale: Acceptance intentionally waits for two complete remote workflows, so polling must be bounded and avoid unnecessary API traffic.

compatibility.rationale: Every workstream uses agent.sh acceptance; the change must preserve existing task provenance and provide deterministic retry behavior for interrupted publication.

concurrency.rationale: Another integration or remote branch update during CI waiting must not cause a stale candidate to overwrite newer harness history.

platform.rationale: The local publisher runs on macOS while the required workflow spans Linux, macOS, and Windows, so API and Git behavior must remain portable and shell-safe.

persistence.rationale: The durable task record stores the verified SHA and remote workflow reference; partial failure must not persist a false done state.

adr.rationale: Remote evidence and protected-branch publication define a cross-workstream acceptance contract that is expensive to reverse.

architecture.rationale: The task changes delivery governance and GitHub integration but does not move production modules or alter runtime dependency direction.

roadmap.rationale: The change strengthens evidence for every milestone without adding product scope or changing roadmap sequencing.

acceptance.note: Accepted by the integration owner after repository verification.
